Rashi on Gittin 14b:10:1.english: This and that [deal] with a healthy person - and his [instruction of] "take" [holech] is not like "acquire" [zechei]:

Rashi on Gittin 14b:10:2.hebrew: הא דמית מקבל בחיי נותן - יחזרו למשלח, דלא זכה בהן מקבל; ואפילו מת הנותן בחזירת השליח, אין כאן משום "מצוה לקיים דברי המת", שקודם מיתתו בטלו דבריו משעת מיתת המקבל:
Rashi on Gittin 14b:10:2.english: This [refers to a case] where the recipient died in the lifetime of the giver - [the funds] are returned to the sender, because the recipient did not acquire them. And even if the giver died during the agent's return, there is no [obligation] here on account of "it is a mitzvah to fulfill the words of the deceased," since prior to his death his words were nullified from the moment of the recipient's death:

Rashi on Gittin 14b:10:3.english: And this [baraita] - which teaches [that it is given] to the heirs of the one to whom [the funds] were sent:

Rashi on Gittin 14b:10:4.hebrew: דמית נותן - לאחר שמסרן לשליח מת, ועדיין מקבל חי. הלכך, משעת מיתת הנותן זכה בהם המקבל, משום דמצוה לקיים דברי המת, ואפילו היה בריא:
Rashi on Gittin 14b:10:4.english: Where the giver died - After he handed them [the funds] over to the agent, he died while the recipient was still alive. Therefore, from the moment of the giver's death, the recipient acquired them, because it is a mitzvah to fulfill the words of the deceased, even if he was healthy:

Rashi on Gittin 14b:12:1.hebrew: ר' יהודה הנשיא כו' - לקמן מפרש מאי פליג איש אומרים:
Rashi on Gittin 14b:12:1.english: Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi, etc. - Later [the Gemara] explains in what [respect] he disagrees with [the opinion of] "some say":

Rashi on Gittin 14b:12:2.english: And here they said - in Babylonia:

Rashi on Gittin 14b:12:3.hebrew: מה שירצה שליח יעשה - לפי מה שראה בדעתו של משלח, אם היתה עינו יפה במתנה זו ואוהב את המקבל ואת בניו:
Rashi on Gittin 14b:12:3.english: What the agent wishes, he may do - According to what [the agent] saw of the sender's intent: whether he was generous with this gift and loved the recipient and his children:

Rashi on Gittin 14b:13:1.hebrew: ת"ק - דלא איירי במת משלח, ואמר יחזרו למשלח:
Rashi on Gittin 14b:13:1.english: The first Tanna - who is not speaking of [a case where] the sender died, and said: Let them return to the sender:

Rashi on Gittin 14b:13:2.hebrew: סבר הולך לאו כזכי דמי - אבל אם מת משלח, לא ידעינן מאי קאמר בה:
Rashi on Gittin 14b:13:2.english: [The first tanna] holds [that] "deliver" is not like "acquire" - But if the sender died, we do not know what he says about it:

Rashi on Gittin 14b:13:3.hebrew: ור' נתן ור' יעקב - הוסיפו על דבריו ואמרו דאפי' מת משלח, לית לן בבריא דמצוה לקיים דברי המת:
Rashi on Gittin 14b:13:3.english: And Rabbi Natan and Rabbi Ya'akov - added to his [the first tanna's] words and said that even if the sender died, we do not hold in [the case of] a healthy person that it is a mitzvah to fulfill the words of the deceased:

Rashi on Gittin 14b:13:4.hebrew: וי"א הולך כזכי דמי - ופליגי אפילו לא מת משלח, ואמילתיה דת"ק [קאי]; תדע, דמדקאמר רבי יהודה הנשיא "מצוה לקיים דברי המת", ש"מ שמעינהו ליש אומרים דתלו טעמייהו ב"הולך כזכי דמי" ואפי' לא מת משלח, ואמר איהו: דוקא מת, דמצוה לקיים דבריו, אבל לא מת — לא, דהולך לאו כזכי דמי:
Rashi on Gittin 14b:13:4.english: And "Some say" [hold that] "Deliver" is like "Acquire" - And they disagree even [if] the sender did not die, and [this] refers to the statement of the Tanna Kamma; know [that this is so], for since Rabbi Yehudah HaNasi said, "It is a mitzva to fulfill the statement of the dead," learn from this that he heard "Some say" basing their reasoning on "Deliver is like Acquire" even [if] the sender did not die, and he [therefore] said: Specifically [when] he died [must it be delivered], because it is a mitzva to fulfill his words, but [when] he did not die — no, because "Deliver" is not like "Acquire":

Rashi on Gittin 14b:15:1.hebrew: מספקא להו - אי הולך כזכי דמי אי לא, ואי מצוה לקיים דברי המת אי לא:
Rashi on Gittin 14b:15:1.english: They are uncertain - whether [saying "take"] is like [saying "acquire"] or not, and whether it is a mitzvah to fulfill [the words of the deceased] or not:

Rashi on Gittin 14b:15:2.english: Shuda - the discretion of the agent:

Rashi on Gittin 14b:15:3.english: Is preferable - to division in a matter that is uncertain:

Rashi on Gittin 14b:16:1.english: In [the case of] a healthy person, no one disagrees - that [saying "deliver"] is not like [saying] "acquire":

Rashi on Gittin 14b:16:2.english: And in the dispute of Rabbi Elazar - who treats a person on his deathbed like a healthy person:

Rashi on Gittin 14b:17:1.hebrew: על פיו - על פי צואתו מחלק נכסיו לבניו, ולא כשאר המורישים שחולקים היורשים בשוה:
Rashi on Gittin 14b:17:1.english: Orally - By his instruction, he divides his property among his sons, and not like others who leave an inheritance, [where] the heirs divide [it] equally:

Rashi on Gittin 14b:17:2.hebrew: בכסף בשטר ובחזקה - שבכך הן נקנים מן הבריא, ושכ"מ נמי לרבי אלעזר אי לאו אקנינהו בהכי, לא מיקנו:
Rashi on Gittin 14b:17:2.english: By money, through a document, or by taking possession - For it is in this manner that they are acquired from a healthy person; and [with regard to] a dangerously ill person as well, according to Rabbi Elazar, if he did not transfer them in this manner, they are not acquired:

Rashi on Gittin 14b:2:1.english: He said to them: Yes - I will return [it]:

Rashi on Gittin 14b:2:2.hebrew: אמר להו לא - כדאמרי' לעיל, אם בא לחזור אינו חוזר:
Rashi on Gittin 14b:2:2.english: [Rabbi Yosei bar Keifar] said to them: No - As we said above, if [the sender] comes to retract, he cannot retract:

Rashi on Gittin 14b:2:3.english: They said to him - to Rabbi Dostai:

Rashi on Gittin 14b:2:4.english: See, Master, what he is doing - that he is not returning [it] to us:

Rashi on Gittin 14b:2:5.hebrew: טב רמו ליה - הרבה הכוהו, לשון מורי. ל"א: טב רמו ליה — יפה ראויות המכות הללו:
Rashi on Gittin 14b:2:5.english: Tav remo leih - They hit him hard — [this is] the wording of my teacher. Another explanation: "Tav remo leih" — these blows are well-deserved:

Rashi on Gittin 14b:3:1.english: Why did you do this? - That you agreed to return [it] immediately:

Rashi on Gittin 14b:4:1.hebrew: הן אמה - אנשי מדות, גבוהים בקומה:
Rashi on Gittin 14b:4:1.english: They are a cubit - Men of [great] stature, tall in height:

Rashi on Gittin 14b:4:2.english: And their hats were a cubit - Even their garments are [more] terrifying than [those of] other people:

Rashi on Gittin 14b:4:3.hebrew: ומדברין מחצייהן - כלומר, קולן עבה, ונראה הדיבור יוצא מטיבורן:
Rashi on Gittin 14b:4:3.english: And they speak from their midpoints - That is to say, their voice is deep, and [their] speech appears to emerge from their navels:

Rashi on Gittin 14b:4:4.english: Arda and Arta and Pili Bereish:

Rashi on Gittin 14b:6:1.english: And did not find him - [meaning] that he had died:

Rashi on Gittin 14b:7:1.hebrew: כזכי דמי - וכיון שזכה בהן בחייו, ינתנו ליורשיו:
Rashi on Gittin 14b:7:1.english: Is like [saying] "Acquire" - and since he [the recipient] acquired them during his lifetime, they are given to his heirs:

Rashi on Gittin 14b:8:1.hebrew: "<abbr title="דכולי עלמא">דכ"ע</abbr> הולך לאו כזכי דמי" <abbr title="גרסינן">גרסי'</abbr>:
Rashi on Gittin 14b:8:1.english: We read [the text]: "Everyone agrees [that] 'Deliver' is not like 'Acquire'":

Rashi on Gittin 14b:8:2.hebrew: בשכיב מרע - שכל זמן שלא חזר בו, דבריו ככתובים וכמסורים, ו"הולך" דידיה "זכי" הוא, ויתנם ליורשי מי שנשתלחו לו, שהרי זכה אביהן בחייו:
Rashi on Gittin 14b:8:2.english: With a person on his deathbed - for as long as he has not retracted, his words are [considered] as written and as delivered, and his "Deliver" is [equivalent to] "Acquire," and he [the agent] shall give them to the heirs of the one to whom they were sent, since their father acquired [them] during his lifetime:

Rashi on Gittin 14b:8:3.hebrew: בבריא - יחזרו למשלח, ד"הולך" לאו כ"זכי" דמי, וזה לא שלחו אלא למקבל ולא ליורשיו:
Rashi on Gittin 14b:8:3.english: With a healthy person - [they] return to the sender, for "deliver" is not like "acquire," and this [sender] sent it only to the recipient and not to his heirs:

Rashi on Gittin 14b:9:1.english: Both this and that [refer to] a person on his deathbed - For his [instruction to] "deliver" is [equivalent to] "acquire":

Rashi on Gittin 14b:9:2.english: This [is a case] where the recipient is - in the world [i.e., alive]:

Rashi on Gittin 14b:9:3.hebrew: בשעת מתן מעות - ושליח זכה בהן מיד, וכשמת זכו יורשיו מכחו:
Rashi on Gittin 14b:9:3.english: At the time of the giving of the money - and the agent acquired them immediately [on the recipient's behalf], and when [the recipient] died, his heirs acquired [them] by virtue of his right:

Rashi on Gittin 14b:9:4.hebrew: הא דליתיה למקבל - שכבר מת, וזה לא היה יודע; נמצאת זכיה בטעות, ולא קנו יורשין:
Rashi on Gittin 14b:9:4.english: That [case] where the recipient is not [alive] - for he had already died and this one [the sender] did not know; [thus,] the acquisition turns out [to have been] in error, and the heirs did not acquire [it]:

Tosafot on Gittin 14b:14:1.hebrew: ור' יהודה הנשיא בשם רבי יעקב אומר הולך לאו כזכי - ואע"ג דרבי אית ליה בפרק התקבל (לקמן גיטין סג.): "הולך ותן לה, זכה לה, התקבל לה — רצה לחזור לא יחזור", דהולך ותן כזכי; התם משום שאמר השליח "אשתך אמרה התקבל לי גטי", דמסתמא על דעת כן נותן לו, כל זמן שאינו אומר בהדיא "אי אפשי שתקבל לה":
Tosafot on Gittin 14b:14:1.english: And Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi says in the name of Rabbi Ya'akov: "Deliver" is not like "Acquire" - And even though Rebbi holds in the chapter [entitled] HaTitkabel (below, Gittin 63a): "[If a husband says,] 'Deliver and give [it] to her,' 'Acquire [it] for her,' [or] 'Accept [it] for her,' [and then] he wishes to retract, he cannot retract" — [implying] that "Deliver and give" is like "Acquire" — there it is because the agent said, "Your wife said, 'Accept my get for me,'" so presumably he gives it to him with that intent, as long as he does not explicitly say, "I do not want you to accept [it] for her":

Tosafot on Gittin 14b:15:1.hebrew: וחכמים אומרים יחלוקו - כל תיקו שבש"ס מפרש בשערים דרבינו האי דחולקים, ואין נראה לר"י, אלא היכא דאשכחן בהדיא "יחלוקו"; דאדרבה, אומרים: אוקי ממונא בחזקת מריה:
Tosafot on Gittin 14b:15:1.english: And the Sages say: They should divide [it] - [Regarding] every teiku in the Talmud, it is explained in the She'arim of Rabbeinu Hai that they divide [it], but this does not seem [correct] to Rabbeinu Yitzchak, [who holds that they divide] only where we explicitly find "they should divide"; for on the contrary, we say: Leave the money in the possession of its [current] owner:

Tosafot on Gittin 14b:15:2.hebrew: וכאן אמרו שודא עדיף - מכאן מדקדק ר"ת, דאין לפרש "שודא" כמו שפי' בקונטרס בפ' הכותב (כתובות פה:) גבי "שניהם קרובים, שניהם שכנים, שניהם תלמידי חכמים — שודא דדייני", דהיינו שידקדק הדיין את מי היה אוהב יותר ולמי היה בדעתו ליתן; וכאן נמי פירש בקונטרס כמו התם. אלא יתן הדיין למי שירצה, כי הכא דקאמר מה שירצה שליח יעשה, וקרי ליה "שודא":
Tosafot on Gittin 14b:15:2.english: And here they said: discretion [shuda] is preferable - From here Rabbeinu Tam infers that one should not explain shuda as Rashi explained in the chapter [entitled] HaKotev (Ketubot 85b), regarding [the case where] "both are relatives, both are neighbors, [or] both are Torah scholars — [it is] shuda dedayanei [the discretion of the judges]," namely, that the judge should carefully investigate whom [the donor] loved more and to whom he intended to give; and here too Rashi explained [it] like there. Rather, the judge may give to whomever he wishes, just as here, where [the Gemara] says that whatever the agent wishes, he may do, and it calls it shuda:

Tosafot on Gittin 14b:17:1.hebrew: ר' אליעזר אומר אחד בריא ואחד כו' - אור"ת דר' אלעזר גרס, דבסיפא פליגי רבי אליעזר ורבי יהושע, רא"א: בשבת דבריו קיימין אבל לא בחול, ורבי יהושע כו', אבל ברישא פליגי בין בחול בין בשבת, מדלא ערבינהו. ועוד, מדפרכי רבנן לרבי אלעזר מאימן של בני רוכל — דלמא בשבת היה, דמודה בה ר"א! ועוד, דקאמר התם: קונים משכיב מרע ואפי' בשבת, ולא לחוש לדברי ר"א; ואי אדר"א קאי, הא מודה הוא בשבת דדבריו קיימים! ואע"ג דר"מ קאמר התם דלר"א בחול דבריו קיימים ולא בשבת, התם לא קאי אר"מ אלא אמתני'. ועוד, דאמר הכא דר"מ כר"א, ו"הולך מנה" משמע דבחול מיירי, ור"מ אית ליה התם דלר"א בחול דבריו קיימים! אלא ודאי ג' מחלוקת בדבר:
Tosafot on Gittin 14b:17:1.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: Both a healthy person and, etc. - Rabbeinu Tam says that we read [the text as] Rabbi Elazar; for in the latter clause [in Bava Batra 156b], Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua disagree — Rabbi Eliezer says, "On Shabbat his words stand, but not on a weekday," and Rabbi Yehoshua [says, etc.] — whereas in the first clause [quoted here] they disagree both on a weekday and on Shabbat, [as proven] from the fact that [the Mishnah] did not combine them. And furthermore, [this is proven] from the fact that the Rabbis challenge Rabbi Elazar from [the incident of] the mother of the sons of Rokhel — [for if it were Rabbi Eliezer,] perhaps it was on Shabbat, in which Rabbi Eliezer concedes! And furthermore, because [Rav Levi] says there [in Bava Batra 156b]: "We perform an act of acquisition from a deathly ill person even on Shabbat, and not [because we need] to be concerned for the words of Rabbi Elazar"; and if [that statement] referred to Rabbi Eliezer, why, he concedes on Shabbat that his words stand! And even though Rabbi Meir says there that according to Rabbi Eliezer, on a weekday his words stand and not on Shabbat, there [Rav Levi] is not referring to Rabbi Meir, rather to the Mishnah [of Rabbi Elazar]. And furthermore, because [the Gemara] says here that Rabbi Meir [holds] like Rabbi Elazar, and [the case of] "deliver a maneh" implies that it is speaking of a weekday — whereas Rabbi Meir holds there that according to Rabbi Eliezer, on a weekday his words stand! Rather, certainly there are three disputes in the matter:

Tosafot on Gittin 14b:8:1.hebrew: הא בשכיב מרע - אור"י: אע"ג דמת מקבל בחיי נותן, ולא קני אלא אחר מיתת נותן, אפ"ה קנו יורשין; דדעת נותן הוא, דכיון שישנו למקבל בשעת מתן מעות, שיזכה המקבל אחר מיתתו, או הוא או יורשיו. ואפי' לא נולדו יורשי מקבל עד אחר מיתת נותן, קנו, אפי' למ"ד "המזכה לעובר לא קנה", דדברי שכיב מרע כשמת כמסורים למקבל משעת נתינת שכיב מרע או אמירתו:
Tosafot on Gittin 14b:8:1.english: This [deals] with a person on his deathbed - Rabbeinu Yitzchak says: Even though the recipient died during the lifetime of the giver, and [the gift] is acquired only after the death of the giver, nevertheless [the recipient's] heirs acquire [it]; for the giver's intention is that, since the recipient exists at the time of the giving of the money, the recipient should acquire [it] after his [the giver's] death — either he or his heirs. And even if the recipient's heirs were not born until after the giver's death, they acquire [it], even according to the one who says, "One who conveys possession to a fetus — [it] does not acquire [it]," because the words of a person on his deathbed, when he dies, are [regarded] as handed over to the recipient from the time of the deathbed person's giving or his statement:
